evidence: 4 ground-truth curves (prop_x=Temperature/K, prop_y=Electrical conductivity/ohm^(-1)*m^(-1)). x-values ~223-399K match the chart's printed x-axis range. 3 of 4 curves have y-values in 61130-103454 ohm^-1*m^-1, consistent with the chart's printed y-axis 'Electrical conductivity sigma, ohm^-1 cm^-1' spanning ~250-1250 after unit conversion (ohm^-1 cm^-1 * 100 = ohm^-1 m^-1). One of the 4 curves has an outlier range (662-1028 ohm^-1*m^-1, ~2 orders of magnitude below the other three) not yet independently reconciled against the chart -- flagged here for a future re-check rather than silently dropped.

14 ground-truth curves (prop_x=Temperature/K, prop_y=ZT/dimensionless), matching the chart's 14 legend entries (HfNiSn, TiNiSn, and 12 superlattice-period samples from 216nm to 1.7nm) exactly. GT x-range 334-488K matches the chart's ~330-500K axis. GT y-range across all 14 curves is 0.0256-0.3410, matching the chart's y-axis (0-0.40) and the visible spread of curves (lowest ~HfNiSn/TiNiSn near 0.03-0.09, highest ~21.6nm reaching ~0.34 at the top-right).

2 ground-truth curves (prop_x=Temperature/K, prop_y=Seebeck coefficient/V*K^(-1)); one is empty (n_points=0, a digitization artifact -- excluded from evaluation since it contributes no points either way). The remaining curve has x-range 298.46-348.30K (25.3-75.15 degC) and y-range 2.667e-5 to 2.212e-4 V/K (26.7-221.2 microV/K), matching the chart's x-axis (25-75/80 degC) and y-axis (Seebeck Coefficient, microV/degC, 0-220ish) closely.

2 ground-truth curves (prop_x=Temperature/K, prop_y=Electrical conductivity/ohm^(-1)*m^(-1)), x-range 872-1174K matches the chart's 600-900 degC axis exactly. y-values 35.4-42.0 ohm^-1*m^-1 (=0.354-0.420 S/cm) match the 'STF35' circle series; y-values 170.4-220.2 ohm^-1*m^-1 (=1.70-2.20 S/cm) match the 'STF50' triangle series, including the STF50 curve's non-monotonic peak-then-decline shape. CAVEAT: the chart's y-axis (Conductivity / S cm^-1) is drawn log-scale, but real_chart_bench's ExtractionTask/PixelCalibration only model log-x, not log-y -- a naive linear-pixel-space model will misjudge this figure's y-values by construction. The pairing itself (this image <-> this ground truth) is verified; scoring against it with the current harness is a separate, known limitation flagged to HQ.
excluded_reason: log-y axis chart; ExtractionTask/PixelCalibration have no y_scale support (design 7.22). HQ decision 2026-08-19: excluded from the real-image evaluation suite until y_scale is implemented as a separate feature task; the pairing itself remains VERIFIED and does not count against the 8-rejected total.

5 ground-truth curves (prop_x=Temperature/K, prop_y=Electrical conductivity/ohm^(-1)*m^(-1)), one per composition x=0.005/0.01/0.05/0.1/0.5. x-range 300-330K matches the chart panel (A)'s T(K) axis exactly. Converting GT y (ohm^-1*m^-1) to the chart's S/cm units (divide by 100) gives near-exact matches to all 5 legend series: x=0.005 -> 0.11-2.07 S/cm (chart ~0-2), x=0.01 -> 1.14-2.13 (chart ~1-2), x=0.05 -> 2.45-4.58 (chart ~2.5-4.6), x=0.1 -> 5.28-9.97 (chart ~5.3-10, the paper's stated max '10 S/cm at 330K'), x=0.5 -> 3.24-6.86 (chart ~3.2-6.9). This is a vector-drawn scatter plot that PDF extraction did not isolate as an embedded raster; captured via the page-render fallback (design 1.2/7.10) instead (p04_page_render_3.png, 1240x1655px at render_dpi=150). IMPORTANT: PyMuPdfPanelSplitter's gutter-based auto-splitter does NOT work on a full article page (it found 4 'panels' that were actually body-text paragraphs, not the 2 chart panels -- confirmed by inspection, and this bug caused the naive-cv baseline to silently score 0.0 against the wrong image region on the first run of this registry). image_path here is therefore a manually-cropped PNG (crop bbox on the full page render: x=[100,620], y=[175,520] for panel A) saved alongside the extracted images, not the raw page render + an automated panel_label. Reproducibility note: re-derivable by re-running PyMuPdfFigureExtractor(render_dpi=150) on this paper's PDF and cropping that exact bbox; this is a known gap (full-page panel splitting) worth fixing in panel_layout.py rather than repeating this manual-crop workaround for future page-render figures.
